name: The Five-Second Rule
blurb: The last cookie hits the floor and a couple invents rules faster than the timer runs out
title: The Five-Second Rule: 30-Second Couple Comedy Script
description: A 30-second vertical comedy script for a couple: the last cookie hits the floor and the five-second rule debate gets out of hand. Free to film.
h1: The Five-Second Rule: a 30-Second Comedy Script for a Couple
logline: Two partners reach for the last cookie and knock it to the floor. One shouts the five-second rule, the other says it is not real, and the rules start multiplying faster than the clock.
setting: A home kitchen at night. Props: a plate, one cookie (plus spares for retakes), a clean floor or a clean tray to drop it on.

roles.name: Jo
roles.note: Adult, any gender, invents rules with total confidence, really wants the cookie.

roles.name: Riley
roles.note: Adult, any gender, Jo's partner, the sensible one who keeps falling for it.

script.action: JO and RILEY reach for the last cookie at the same time. It falls. Both freeze.
Riley picks the cookie up. Jo grabs Riley's wrist.

script.say: If nobody's looking, the timer resets. Close your eyes.

script.action: Riley sighs and closes their eyes. Jo closes theirs. Silence. A crunch.
Riley opens one eye. The cookie is gone. Jo is chewing, eyes still shut.

script.say: Can't prove it. Nobody was looking.

body: Shoot vertical 9:16 on a tripod or propped against the fridge at chest height, so the two-shot keeps both faces and the plate in frame. Overhead kitchen light at night is fine; add a lamp from the side to soften faces. Drop the cookie onto a clean tray or freshly wiped floor and keep spares, because the drop rarely lands right the first time. Two to five takes of the full run, then pick up the inserts separately.

ul: Jo states every new rule as plain fact, with no smile. The faster and calmer the rule, the bigger the laugh.
Riley is right every time and still loses. Play mild outrage, never real anger, so it stays a couple joke.
Pause for one beat after elbow counts. Riley's silent look sells the absurdity.
Hold the eyes-closed silence for two full seconds before the crunch. The quiet is what makes the sound funny.
Jo keeps eyes closed through the last line. Opening them would break the logic of the punchline.
Swap the cookie for the last dumpling, a slice of fruit or a piece of chocolate, and set it at a picnic or a dinner table.
Play it as two roommates, two siblings or a parent and an adult child; the rules war works for any pair who share food.
Part-two hook: Riley drops the next cookie on purpose, shouts a new rule first, and Jo is outplayed at their own game.

faq.a: Not as science. Food can pick up germs the moment it touches a surface, so drop the cookie on a clean tray for filming and use a fresh one for the actual bite.

faq.q: Can I use it on my couple channel and earn money from it?
faq.a: Yes. It is free under CC BY 4.0, including monetised channels. Credit "Script: cv.cm" in your caption.

faq.q: How do I make it longer than 30 seconds?
faq.a: Add one more rule between the elbow and the eyes-closed beats, such as a birthday bonus or a blowing-on-it extension, and keep each new rule shorter and more confident than the last.
